hypothesis: In North Sea plaice, Fulton-type condition (weight at fixed length) declines from about November to March/April and recovers from May/June to November, and the seasonal minimum coincides with the spawning season (maturity stage "spawning"/"spent"), so that spawning timing can be inferred from length-weight alone.
pass_criterion: Using DATRAS plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) individual records with length, individual weight, sex and maturity, fit log(W) = a + b*log(L) + month effect (or quarter effect) for mature fish. PASS if (i) the month-effect minimum falls in Feb-Apr and the maximum in Aug-Dec, (ii) the amplitude (max minus min predicted weight at fixed length) is at least 10% and the month term is significant (p<0.01), and (iii) the month of lowest condition is within 1 month of the month with the highest proportion of spawning/spent-stage fish (or the minimum shows in mature fish with an amplitude at least twice that of immature fish).
fail_criterion: FAIL if the amplitude of the seasonal weight-at-length cycle is under 5%, or the minimum falls outside Jan-May, or the minimum lies more than 2 months from the peak of spawning-stage fish, or immature fish show a seasonal amplitude equal to or greater than mature fish, which would indicate the cycle is not caused by spawning.
interpretation: Thompson's "weight at unchanging length" is mapped to the residual of log individual weight regressed on log length (relative condition). "Bulk" is taken as weight. "Spawning" is mapped to the maturity-stage code in the survey records. Caveat: DATRAS surveys are mostly in quarters 1 and 3 (and some in quarter 4), so monthly resolution is coarse, and the data may only cover part of the cycle. The claim that the cycle is "wholly" caused by spawning is tested only through the mature versus immature contrast. Gonad weight and feeding effects are not separated. The "spawning season can be determined from length and weight alone" part is tested by agreement with the maturity-stage record.

dataset.name: DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys)
dataset.publisher: ICES (International Council for the Exploration of the Sea)
dataset.why_it_fits: Public bottom-trawl survey data with individual-fish biological records for North Sea plaice. Fields to use: species/Valid_Aphia, LngtClass, IndWgt, Sex, Maturity, Month, Quarter, Year, StatRec. Raw data are downloadable and available through web services and the icesDATRAS R package. Caveat: the fetched landing page did not list the field names; these come from my knowledge of the DATRAS exchange format and must be checked against the download page. IndWgt may be sparsely recorded.
